saw_lines: Skincare buyers stick to one routine for months, so the first product that earns trust decides the whole basket.
So the sale is won or lost in the first line, before a buyer sees any reason to trust you.
Your 5 of 20 copy ads use claim words, which risk reach, so replace each claim with what customers noticed in week one.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 27 Oct 2026
points: 5 of 20 copy ads use claim words like clinically and guaranteed results, which invites review limits on your strongest ads. Replace each claim with what customers noticed in week one, then test three variations of your best ad.
None of your 30 ads shows a proof number, so buyers have no reason to trust you before the click. Pull one real figure, such as your review count or orders shipped, and lead the next batch with it.

3 of 20 copy ads are creator style posts, with a code, #ad or @mention, run from your brand page. Ask those creators for whitelisting access, run their posts from their own accounts, and cut three variations with fresh openers.

5 of 20 copy ads open on “stopped believing the promises of...”, while the rest each open differently. Test two new angles against that opener, such as your return policy and a subscription option, which none of your ads mention yet.

ads_1: Customer week one results and a return policy angle, tested against the current opener
soc_1: Brand social strategy across Facebook, Instagram and YouTube
